checkpoints.name: logic_correctness
checkpoints.detail: LLM-judge MATERIAL gaps: Implementation and docs are broadly aligned on firing conditions (explicit pass=false and mean-below-floor), but diverge significantly on multi-evaluator handling (cap not disclosed), per-evaluator thresholds (advertised in metadata but unexplained in content), higher_is_better asymmetry (not documented), and rolling-window semantics (docs say rolling, code does all-execution aggregation).. Gaps: Backend implements two distinct APIs: DetectGroundingFailureWithThresholds (legacy first-match-wins) and DetectGroundingFailureAllMatchesWithThresholds (multi-match). Customer docs only describe the current behavior (all matches per G2 wave) without mentioning that legacy first-match behavior still exists in backward-compat code path.; Backend comment states 'real executions evaluate ~1-5 evaluators' but caps output at MaxGroundingFailureMatchesPerExecution=20. Customer docs do not disclose this cap or explain what happens when an execution has >20 distinct (evaluator, metric) failures.; Backend implements per-evaluator threshold overrides (PerEvaluatorFloors map, Theme B extensions wave, closes G3) with fallback to MeanFloor. Customer docs mention 'per-project tunable mean_floor' in metadata but the main article text does not explain per-evaluator override capability or how to configure it.; Backend code shows mean_floor defaults to 0.5 and is clamped to [0.0, 1.0] with fallback to 0.5 on invalid config. Customer docs state 'default 0.5' but do not document the clamping behavior or invalid-config fallback.; Backend only computes mean score for evaluators with higher_is_better=true; inverse metrics are explicitly banked ('inverse metrics need their own threshold semantics'). Customer docs do not explain this asymmetry or what happens to lower_is_better evaluators.

Gaps: Implementation includes 'validation_failed' as a failure terminal status, but customer docs list 'tool_failures' and 'validator_failures' as examples of child failure groups without mentioning 'validation_failed' specifically; Implementation's failureTerminalStatuses explicitly excludes 'halted', but the customer docs state 'halted status is explicitly excluded' referring to operator-driven failures, yet the playbook says child failures include 'crashes', 'timeout', and 'validation_failed' without clarifying the halted exclusion scope; Customer docs claim 'time_budget' is a failure terminal status that triggers cascading_failure detection, but the Go implementation's failureTerminalStatuses only includes 'crashed', 'timeout', and 'validation_failed' — 'time_budget' is not present; Implementation filters rows where ChildEndedAt is nil (conservatively keeps them), but this defensive behavior is not documented in customer-facing copy which should explain when cascades fire without complete timing data

Gaps: Playbook states detector finds '2-cycles only' and 'v1 does not implement' longer cycles, but implementation actually implements Tarjan SCC for N≥3 cycles as a fallback when no 2-cycle exists; Playbook says 'A note on detection scope' warns customers that longer cycles are 'possible in principle but rarer in practice' and 'v1 covers the common case', but this is outdated — the current implementation (v2) actively detects N≥3 cycles via Tarjan when 2-cycles are absent; Customer docs TSX page correctly describes both 2-cycle and Tarjan SCC detection ('N≥3 cycles via Tarjan'), but the canonical playbook document contradicts this by claiming v1 does not implement N≥3 detection; Playbook remediation advice focuses on 2-cycle tie-breaker strategies and does not mention Tarjan-detected N-cycle scenarios, leaving customers without guidance on how to break 3+ cycles beyond the generic data-dependency restructuring point

checkpoints.name: logic_correctness
checkpoints.detail: LLM-judge MATERIAL gaps: The implementation and customer-facing docs have material inconsistencies in the canonical error class vocabulary, the filtering logic for which classes aggregate cross-tenant, provider coverage claims, and undocumented per-project and tier-aware threshold behavior.. Gaps: Go code defines ErrorClassRateLimited, ErrorClassQuotaExhausted, ErrorClassInternalError, ErrorClassServiceUnavailable, ErrorClassTimeout, ErrorClassInvalidAPIKey, ErrorClassClientError, ErrorClassUnknown as canonical classes, but TSX docs list only: rate_limited, quota_exhausted, service_unavailable, auth_failed, invalid_request, timeout, connection_error, content_filter. The sets do not match.; Go implementation uses IsProviderSideErrorClass() to filter which error classes trigger cross-tenant aggregation (ProviderSideErrorClasses set), but neither the playbook nor TSX docs disclose that some error classes are explicitly excluded from provider_incident detection. The playbook discusses auth_error and rate_limited as if they always aggregate, but the code may filter them based on ProviderSideErrorClasses membership.; TSX docs claim coverage for 'Cohere', 'Gemini', but Go code and playbook refer only to 'Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, Mistral' in comments. Cohere is mentioned in TSX but not in the Go source material.; Go code hardcodes MinTenantsForProviderIncident = 2 as default, and playbook confirms 'defaults to firing when at least two distinct tenants are affected.' TSX docs say 'min_tenants (default 2)' but also mention 'Per-project min_tenants threshold + tier-aware caps' in metadata, implying per-project overrides and tier-based caps that are not documented or implemented in the visible Go code.

checkpoints.name: logic_correctness
checkpoints.detail: LLM-judge MATERIAL gaps: The implementation and customer-facing docs have material inconsistencies around the explicit timeout field name (response_kind vs status), the all-matches behavior (both signatures now returned per G3 wave), and missing documentation of the per-project FireModes tuning feature.. Gaps: Implementation uses response_kind == "timeout" as the explicit timeout signal, but customer docs TSX page states status="timed_out" as the completion argument. These are different field names and values.; Canonical playbook and implementation both document "explicit timeout wins" priority, but customer docs TSX page says "Explicit-timeout-wins is the correct priority" without clarifying that when BOTH fire on the same execution, both signatures are now returned (per DetectHITLTimeoutAllMatches and hitl_timeout.G3 wave). The TSX docs create ambiguity about whether explicit suppresses SLA-exceeded.; Implementation includes per-project FireModes tuning (hitl_timeout.G4 wave) allowing customers to restrict detection to only "explicit" or only "sla_exceeded" modes. This capability is not mentioned in either the canonical playbook or customer docs TSX page.; Customer docs TSX page references "status=\"timed_out\"" in the example code snippet, but the implementation code comments consistently use response_kind="timeout". This is a field/value mismatch in the documented API surface.
